about.title: About & how to use
about.intro: Flyball Team Tracker helps your club plan trainings and competitions: who's coming, which dogs run which tasks, and how your race lineups are built.

tasks.title: Tasks
items: Tasks are laid out on a grid of rows and columns - drag a card to reorder it, or move it into a different cell.
The board shows your club’s plan for its next training session. Pick an event at the top to see which of its dogs are marked present.
A task can list dogs directly, or link to a team lineup instead - tap a linked task itself (not one of its dogs) to see and edit that lineup's cross-pass timing.
Tap any dog on a task to see its notes and cross-passes, same as on My Dogs - edit them if it's your own dog or you're a trainer, otherwise just view.

calendar.title: Calendar
items: Every event your club has scheduled - trainings, competitions, seminars, meetings - shows up under two tabs: Upcoming (soonest first) and Past (most recent first).
Narrow the list to a date range with the From/To filters, and page through it once there are more events than fit on one screen.
Expand an event's details to mark your own (or your dogs') attendance: tap a name to cycle it through present, absent, and unset.
Tapping a push notification about an event jumps straight here and scrolls to it, whatever page it's on.

myDogs.title: My Dogs
items: Each of your dogs gets a card here - add general notes, and manage its cross passes (who it runs on, its starting position, and timing).
Cross passes recorded here are your own record, separate from the cross passes set inside your team's lineups - unless you turn on syncing for a dog in Settings, which keeps the two in step.
If your trainer has set a jump height for a dog, it shows on its card here.

teams.title: Teams
items: A team is a pool of up to 6 dogs your club can build race lineups from.
Each team can have several lineups - a lineup is an ordered set of dogs for a race, with cross-pass timing between each dog.
A lineup's name shows its jump height in brackets, e.g. "Super lineup (25cm)" - automatically the lowest jump height among its dogs (a dog with no height set counts as 35cm).
Once every dog in a lineup has a time recorded, its net time shows underneath - the sum of the dogs' own times, not the team's actual (faster) race time.

resources.title: Resources
items: A shared list of external links for your club - its Facebook page, an event spreadsheet, or anything else worth keeping handy.
Anyone in the club can add, edit, or remove a link - not just trainers.
Tap a link to open it in a new tab; use the pencil and trash icons to edit or remove it.

settings.title: Settings
items: Switch the app's language between Polish and English at any time - your choice is saved to your account.
Change your own password here at any time, with your current password to confirm it's really you.

For each of your own dogs, there are two independent cross-pass syncing options: keep its timing in sync across every lineup it runs in after the same dog, and/or keep it in sync with its standalone My Dogs cross-passes.
Turn on push notifications to get a nudge when a new event is created, and a reminder if you haven't marked your attendance ~24h before one starts.

trainerSection.title: Trainer tools
trainerSection.intro: As a trainer, you also get a dedicated panel for managing your club's data:
items: Tasks - the same drag-and-drop board, plus create, edit and delete. The board is scoped to the session picked at the top, so you can plan future trainings ahead of time; the nearest upcoming one is selected by default. On an empty session board, "Copy plan from previous session" seeds it from your most recently planned session. Use "Download PDF" for an A4-formatted printable copy of the plain board members see - pick "Save as PDF" in the print dialog, or print it directly.

Dogs, Dog tasks, Users - manage your club's dogs (including each dog's jump height), the task types they can be assigned, and your club's members. Open a member's card to reset their password if they're locked out - you'll get a one-time temporary password to pass along to them.

Events - create trainings, competitions, seminars, and meetings for your club; the soonest upcoming one is pinned at the top here too. The bell icon on an event immediately sends an attendance-reminder push to anyone who hasn't marked yet, regardless of the usual ~24h timing. Toggle "Repeats weekly" to create a whole block of sessions at once - pick the weekdays and an end date (up to 3 months out) and each session is created as its own independent event, with its own attendance.
Teams - build and edit teams and their lineups for your whole club, not just your own dogs.

EJS Stats - upload a competition’s EJS export file(s) (.xls or .xlsx) for run counts, fault/ok rates, effectiveness, average times, comparison charts and a pass-outcome breakdown. View it by whole club, by team, by lineup or by dog, and switch the scope between "My club" and "All clubs" to see opponents too. "All competitions together" aggregates every import, with a per-file breakdown on the dog and team tabs. Confirming an import replaces ALL of that competition’s existing data, so upload every day’s file together if there’s more than one.
Features - turn off the parts of the app your club doesn’t use, like Teams & Lineups, Cross-passes, Events/Calendar, EJS Stats, or the Dog Tasks catalog.

trainerWorkflow.title: Getting started as a trainer
trainerWorkflow.intro: The order that actually works, first time through:

addDogs.title: Add your dogs
addDogs.body: Go to Dogs and add every dog in your club - a team can only pick from dogs that already exist.

buildTeams.title: Build a team
buildTeams.body: Go to Teams and create a pool of up to 6 dogs your club races with.

buildLineups.title: Build a lineup
buildLineups.body: Inside that team, order 4 dogs into a lineup - jump height is worked out automatically from the shortest dog.

addTasks.title: Add tasks
addTasks.body: Go to Tasks and plan training on the drag-and-drop board - pick dogs directly, or link a task to a whole lineup.

setCrossPasses.title: Set cross-pass times
setCrossPasses.body: At training, open a lineup-linked task to edit the handoff timing between neighboring dogs.

pitch.intro: Flyball Team Tracker helps a club plan trainings and competitions: who's coming, which dogs run which tasks, and how race lineups are built.

addDogs.title: Add your dogs to the club
addDogs.body: Every dog gets its own card - notes, jump height, cross-passes.

buildTeams.title: Build teams and lineups
buildTeams.body: A pool of up to 6 dogs per team, any number of lineups, each in its own running order.

addTasks.title: Add tasks
addTasks.body: A drag-and-drop board, planned around which dogs are actually at training.

setCrossPasses.title: At training, set cross-pass times
setCrossPasses.body: Link a task to a lineup and edit the timing between neighboring dogs right from that task - once every dog has a time, the lineup's net time totals itself.

liveSync.title: Everyone sees it live
liveSync.body: A lineup or attendance change shows up for everyone with the app open, right away.

alsoIncludes.title: Also included
items: Click any dog on a task to see (and, if it's yours or you're a trainer, edit) its notes and cross-passes.
Trainers can import a competition’s EJS export (.xls/.xlsx) for club, team, lineup and dog stats - your own club or opponents’ - plus comparison charts and a pass-outcome breakdown.
Trainers can download the task board as a printable A4 PDF.

pitch.needCode: You'll need a club code from your trainer to sign up.
